title: The Erdős-Faudree Problems and the Isolate-Free Core
summary: In 1981, Erdős and Faudree asked whether there exists an infinite family of graphs $G_N$ on $N$ vertices with $Δ(G_N)<N-1$ and $\sri(G_N)=1$, and whether every family with $|V(G_N)|=N$ and $Δ(G_N)<c$ for some fixed constant $c$ must satisfy $\sri(G_N)\to 0$. We show first that the literal forms of the two questions are controlled entirely by isolated vertices: for every nonempty graph $G$, the whole sequence $\bigl(\sr(tK_2,G)\bigr)_{t\ge 1}$ depends only on the isolate-free core $\core(G)$.
